headline: SHAREHOLDER VOTE CLEARS CRITICAL METALS / EUROPEAN LITHIUM MERGER — WA Court Oct 26, Close Expected Nov 5
snippet: European Lithium securityholders voted to approve Critical Metals Corp's acquisition on October 22, clearing the way for a Western Australian court hearing on October 26 and an expected implementation date of November 5. European Lithium holds the Wolfsberg lithium project in Austria — one of the few hard-rock lithium deposits in Europe — and the combined entity is positioning for strategic relevance in the EU's battery supply chain independence push as Brussels accelerates domestic critical mineral sourcing.

headline: ALPHA DRILLS 18m at 15.33 g/t AU at Aburna — Enlarged 8,910m 2026 Program Closes Out Well Ahead of Original Target
snippet: Alpha Exploration Ltd. (TSXV: ALEX) completed its 2026 drill program at Aburna with 8,910 metres total — significantly more than planned after early results including 18 metres at 15.33 g/t gold justified budget expansion. Grades of that calibre in a first-pass drill program suggest a well-mineralised system rather than an isolated high-grade zone; full assay results from the expanded holes are pending and will determine whether the Aburna project advances to a maiden resource estimate.

headline: DISCOVERY MINING EXTENDS DOME 600m SOUTH — 51.87 g/t Au Over 1.8m Confirms Large Open-Pit Scale
snippet: Discovery Mining (TSX: DSV) extended mineralization 600 metres to the south at its Dome project with intercepts including 51.87 g/t gold over 1.8 metres and 2.34 g/t over 14.3 metres, continuing to build the case for large-scale open-pit potential. The lateral step-out at that magnitude alongside a broad envelope of lower-grade mineralisation is consistent with bulk-mineable geometry — the type of orebody that attracts producer attention in a $4,000 gold market where development-stage acquisitions are accelerating.

headline: LIBERTY GOLD LAUNCHES BLACK PINE DRILL CAMPAIGN — 7,417m in 29 RC Holes Targets Oxide Gold Expansion in Idaho
snippet: Liberty Gold Corp (TSX: LGD) reported initial results from 7,417 metres drilled across 29 reverse circulation holes at Black Pine, Idaho, targeting a northern extension of the oxide gold resource beyond the existing pit boundary. Black Pine is a heap-leach candidate in a proven Idaho oxide-gold district; any resource addition outside the current pit boundary improves project economics without adding processing capital requirements, making the northern extension the project's highest-value exploration target.

headline: KINGFISHER METALS WRAPS 13,551m HWY 37 SEASON — 212m STOCKWORK ZONE in Final Holes Adds Scale to Golden Triangle Play
snippet: Kingfisher Metals Corp (TSXV: KFR) completed 13,551 metres in 24 holes at its HWY 37 project in British Columbia's Golden Triangle, reporting a stockwork mineralised interval over 212 metres in hole HW-26-028 in the program's final batch. A 212-metre stockwork intercept signals bulk-mineable porphyry geometry rather than narrow veins, which is the architecture needed to attract a major producer to the deal table; HWY 37 sits in the same structural corridor as several of the district's largest deposits.

headline: PHOENIX TAILINGS to Build $375M RARE EARTH PLANT in New York — Largest Private US REE Processing Investment to Date
snippet: Phoenix Tailings announced a $375 million rare earth separation and processing facility in Rochester, New York — one of the most significant private investments in US rare earth processing capacity, targeting separation and metallic conversion of REEs for defence and clean-energy end uses. The plant directly addresses the supply-chain bottleneck that exists even when domestic REE mining succeeds: the US has historically sent ore to China for separation, and without domestic processors, mining independence from China remains incomplete.

headline: CHINA REE EXPORT PAUSE ENDS NOV 10 — No Extension Published; Heavy REE Licensing Rules Remain Active
snippet: China's suspension of its October 2025 rare earth export controls expires November 10, 2026, with no extension published by Beijing; the US-China truce text runs to January 10, 2027 on the American side but Beijing has not published matching language. The April 2025 licensing requirement covering seven heavy rare earths — including dysprosium and terbium used in high-performance permanent magnets — remains in force regardless of the November 10 outcome, sustaining supply-chain risk for defence contractors and EV motor manufacturers dependent on Chinese REE processing.

headline: 134 NEW LITHIUM MINES NEEDED by 2050 — Benchmark Puts Investment Gap at $150B as Spot Prices Sit Near Multi-Year Lows
snippet: Benchmark Mineral Intelligence estimates the equivalent of 134 new lithium mines — and over $150 billion of investment under its upside scenario — are needed to meet EV-driven demand between now and 2050, arriving as spot lithium carbonate and spodumene prices sit at multi-year lows near US$1,700 per tonne. The structural paradox is sharp: today's depressed prices suppress the incentive to build the mines that will be desperately under-supplied within a decade, a setup that historically precedes violent price reversals when inventory destocking ends and demand commitments land on producers.

headline: APOGEE MINERALS BUYS KNIFE LAKE COPPER CLAIMS from Eagle Plains — Saskatchewan Footprint Expands Ahead of Drill Results
snippet: Apogee Minerals Inc. acquired adjacent mineral claims from Eagle Plains Resources at the Knife Lake copper project in Saskatchewan, expanding the land package while LME copper prices remain near multi-year highs and before drilling demonstrates the deposit's along-strike direction. Consolidating adjacent ground early in the exploration cycle is a textbook low-cost move: once drill results demonstrate deposit geometry, land prices in any district typically reprice sharply upward, so the time to buy is before the drilling tells you which way to look.

headline: GUYANA GOLD RUSH ACCELERATES — Nine Foreign Mining Deals in 2026 as Explorers Race the Stabroek Belt Land Grab
snippet: Foreign companies struck nine deals for Guyanese mining properties in 2026, including a Golden Shield letter agreement in October, as explorers rush to secure ground in South America's fastest-developing mining jurisdiction. Guyana's Precambrian craton hosts known gold, copper, and bauxite deposits historically underexplored due to access and infrastructure constraints; the nine-deal pace represents a sharp acceleration from prior years and suggests land acquisition costs will move meaningfully higher before the district's first major exploration-stage discoveries are announced.

headline: GOLD FACES PRE-FOMC DISTRIBUTION SETUP — GoldSeek: Trump Fiscal Strategy Shaping Into Oct 28 Sell-Off Trigger
snippet: A GoldSeek analysis published October 19 argues gold faces elevated sell-off risk into the October 28 FOMC decision as the Trump administration's fiscal and monetary strategy crystallises and creates binary uncertainty about Fed Chair Warsh's response; the author identifies a distribution pattern in gold futures that has historically preceded 5–10% corrections surrounding Fed decision days. The piece adds context to Wednesday's unusual triple-metals selloff: if professional money is positioning short ahead of FOMC, the retail investor community sitting in unhedged gold equity is carrying the most risk into a decision that could cut either way.

headline: RECORD MARGINS, HISTORIC DISCOUNT: Gold Miners' Q2'26 Fundamentals Show Lowest P/CF in a Decade
snippet: Adam Hamilton's GoldSeek analysis of Q2 2026 gold miner fundamentals finds the major producers posted near-record earnings even as gold pulled back from its January peak, yet the sector now trades at its lowest price-to-cash-flow and P/NAV in at least a decade — the widest disconnect Hamilton has measured between operating profitability and equity valuation. The setup implies a potential violent re-rating when Q3 results hit the income statement and investors see two consecutive quarters of $3,000+ gold margins where previously only gold's spot chart was visible.
